segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Welcome to this podcast about the Sheepmarket, which is one of the oldest parts of the city.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As its name suggests, there was originally a market here where farmers brought their sheep, but now it’s been redeveloped into a buzzing, vibrant area of the city, which is also home to one of the city’s fastest-growing communities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The nearby university has always meant the area’s popular with students, who come in to enjoy the lively nightlife, but now graduates embarking on careers in the worlds of fashion and design are buying up the new apartments recently built here to replace the small houses where the market workers used to live. The narrow old side streets are great places for finding original pictures, jewellery and ceramics which won’t break the bank, as well as local produce like fruit and vegetables.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’s also lots of pavement cafes where you can have a coffee and watch tourists from all over the world go by.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The oldest buildings in the area are on the main streets, including the city’s first department store, built in the 1880s, which is still open today.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Sheepmarket is a centre for fashion, and there’s a policy of encouraging new young designers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Young Fashion competition is open to local young people who are passionate about fashion.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This year they’ve been asked to design an outfit based on ideas from the music and technology that’s part of their everyday life, using both natural and man-made fibres.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The garments will be judged by a panel of experts and fashion designers, and the winning entries will be modelled at a special gala evening.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Parking at the Sheepmarket is easy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are plenty of pay and display car parking spaces on the roadsides which are fine if you just want to stay for an hour or two, but if you want to spend the day there it’s better to park in one of the four underground car parks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s not expensive and if you can present a receipt from one of the local stores, you’ll not be charged at all.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: After six pm many of the car parks have a flat rate which varies but it is usually very reasonable. ————————- The Sheepmarket is one of the main centres for art and history in the whole of the country.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you look at our map, you’ll see some of the main attractions there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most visitors start from Crawley Road, at the bottom of the map.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Reynolds House is one of the oldest houses in the city, and is open to the public.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s on the north side of Crawley Road, next to the footpath that leads to the public gardens. The area’s particularly interesting for its unusual sculptures.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Thumb’s is just what its name suggests, but it’s about 10 metres high.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You’ll see it on Hill Road, across the road from the Bank. The Museum’s got a particularly fine collection of New Zealand landscapes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s on the east side of the Sheepmarket, on City Road.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s on the other side of the road from the public gardens, immediately facing the junction with Hill Road. The Contemporary Art Gallery is on a little road that leads off Station Square, not far from the public gardens.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The road ends at the gallery – it doesn’t go anywhere else.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That’s open every day except Mondays.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Warner Gallery specialises in 19th-century art.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s on City Road, near the junction with Crawley Road, on the same side of the road as the public gardens.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s open on weekdays from 9 to 5, and entry is free.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Finally, if you’re interested in purchasing high quality artwork, the place to go is Nucleus.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You need to go from Crawley Road up through Station Square and east along Hill Road until you get to a small winding road turning off.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Go up there and it’s on your right – if you get to City Road you’ve gone too far.
